children.approach: The step from the window lemma to the range statement of cor:range, machine-checked. card_le_card_of_window_labels: a Finset S of integers inside Finset.Ico p (p+N) whose residues mod N all lie in a Finset L of residue classes has S.card <= L.card -- the interface through which the abacus enters the argument, with the abacus itself NOT formalised. uglovLabel (c : Fin n) (d : Fin l) : ZMod (n*l) is Uglov's label as a residue, from k = c + n(d-1) - N mu (math/9905196, eq. eq:kcd of sec:conv), 0-based here against the paper's 1-based, which is a constant shift of ZMod N and so affects nothing about distinctness or counting. Its two axis-wise injectivities give the two halves of cor:range: card_le_sub_one_of_runner_ne (beads in the window with first coordinate c and runner != d number at most l-1, i.e. a <= l-1) and card_le_sub_one_of_residue_ne (beads on runner d with first coordinate != c number at most n-1 = e-1, i.e. h <= e-1). Window hypothesis stated for the half-open Ico p (p+N), which CONTAINS the paper's open window (p, p+N), so a caller holding the paper's hypothesis applies these directly. WHAT IS STILL ON PAPER, and is the exact gap to cor:range as stated: (1) the coordinate change -- the paper's a is #{d'>d : kappa in M_d'} + #{d'<d : kappa+e in M_d'} in the kappa-coordinate, and its equality with the k-coordinate window count is the last paragraph of the proof of thm:closed (solving eq:kcd to get mu'=mu for d'>d and mu'=mu-1 for d'<d); here S IS the k-coordinate set and the change of coordinate is assumed. (2) Surjectivity: only 'at most once' is proved, because only that half bounds; the 'exactly once' half of the sec:conv remark is what would make the bounds ATTAINED, and is not established. (3) The lower bounds 0<=a, 0<=h, trivial for a cardinality, are not stated.
